about: One record per check. Every record names its authority, so every finding does.

kind 'pattern': a Python regex run on normalized text (curly quotes made straight, runs of whitespace made one space). 'fix' is a re.sub template, or null when the fix needs a fact the writer must supply. {reporter} in a pattern stands for any reporter form the checker reads (florida.json's reporter tables).
kind 'table': patterns built from a table in florida.json ('table' names it).
kind 'logic': needs dates, numbers, or the whole document; 'logic' names the function in scripts/fl_check.py that runs it.
tier 'bluebook': the check is the Bluebook system's, which 9.800(p) sends citations to; Rule 9.800 has no short forms, so Id., supra, and short case cites are checked against the Indigo Book.
kind 'none': a subdivision with nothing mechanical to check; kept so every subdivision has a record and the agent knows to judge it.
severity 'error': clearly departs from Rule 9.800's form. 'check': probably wrong, or right in some contexts; the agent decides.
examples.match must produce the finding; examples.no_match must not. Every record with examples is tested against them offline (logic records as of 2026-10-01).
summarize: true reports one finding per distinct text and fix, with a count and every location, instead of one finding per occurrence.
